stimuli.title: Farah, Nisha, Pia, Bina, Isha, Riya, Kiran, Esha sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. For reference only, seats 1–8 run clockwise. For a centre-facing person, left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise.

Use all the following clues:
• Riya occupies seat 2.
• Bina sits 3 place(s) to the left of Pia.
• Pia sits 1 place(s) to the left of Nisha.
• Esha sits 1 place(s) to the left of Riya.
• Kiran sits 1 place(s) to the left of Pia.
• Isha sits 5 place(s) to the left of Nisha.

stimuli.title: Hema, Esha, Nisha, Bina, Lata, Farah, Ovi, Pia occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.

Use all the following clues:
• Pia occupies floor 2, flat A.
• The floor numbers of Esha and Farah differ by 3.
• Esha and Pia live in different flat letters.
• Bina lives below Ovi.
• Nisha lives below Farah.
• Bina and Pia live in different flat letters.
• Lata and Ovi live in different flat letters.
• Ovi lives in Flat A.
• The floor numbers of Hema and Lata differ by 2.

stimuli.title: Nisha, Bina, Charu, Tara, Meera, Aditi, Farah, Uma attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Uma occupies March 7.
• Exactly 2 occupied positions separate Aditi and Farah in the stated order.
• Exactly 6 occupied positions separate Nisha and Uma in the stated order.
• Charu attends in March.
• Exactly 3 occupied positions separate Nisha and Bina in the stated order.
• Aditi occupies an even-numbered position in the stated order.
• Tara comes before Meera in the stated order.
stimuli.solution: March 7: Uma; March 21: Charu; April 7: Farah; April 21: Bina; May 7: Tara; May 21: Aditi; June 7: Meera; June 21: Nisha

questions.stem:
Statements: No accounts is a lockers. Some lockers are files. All files are branches.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are branches.
II. Some branches are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are lockers. Some lockers are files. All files are branches.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are branches.
II. No lockers is a branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are lockers. All lockers are files. No files is a branches.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are not lockers.
II. No lockers is a branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some accounts are lockers. All lockers are files. No files is a branches.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are files.
II. Some lockers are branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: T = P > Q > V = W.
Conclusions: I. T ≤ Q   II. P > T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: U > X > T > W = P.
Conclusions: I. X ≥ W   II. W ≤ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. X > T   II. W ≥ S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. S ≤ U   II. U ≥ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital banking rural = pa vo ni
digital growth access = mi pa su
banking growth savings = vo mi ka
rural access savings = ka ni su
digital banking savings = ka vo pa
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: mi. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: digital = pa, banking = vo, rural = ni, growth = mi, access = su, savings = ka.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 47 km east, turns left and walks 48 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Net displacement is 36 km east and 48 km north. By Pythagoras, √(36² + 48²) = 60 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 63 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 51 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: D is the mother of F. A is the son of F. C is the father of F. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. C is a parent of F, and A is F’s son. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of H. H is the mother of F. E is the father of C and H. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother H. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of F. F is the father of E. A is the son of E. C is the sister of F. How is F related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of E, and E is A’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 37 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 17. New front rank = 18+3 = 21. Back rank = 37 − 21 + 1 = 17.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 20th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 20+4 = 24. Back rank = 52 − 24 + 1 = 29.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹900. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1250. Selling price = 900 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1250.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 24 days and B in 36 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 17.33. Use 72 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 72 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 273 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 17 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹23000 for 12 months. B invests ₹92000 for 7 months. Total profit is ₹152000. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 106400. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 28. B’s share = total × 28/(40) = 106400.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹33000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 82.5. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 33000 × (5/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 95 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 19. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 19.

questions.stem: The average of 15 numbers is 48. One number, 60, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 135. Total increases by 15 × 5. New number = 60 + 75.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 84 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 8 = 84; x = 19, so father = 57.

questions.stem: A train of length 120 m crosses a 120 m platform at 72 km/h. Find crossing time in seconds (to two decimals).
A village has 4900 registered customers. This increases by 10% in year 1 and decreases by 10% in year 2. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 4851. Apply successive factors: 4900 × 110/100 × 90/100.
